permissions._comment_qa_commands: The `manage.py` entries in the allow list are dev-database-only QA commands. The danger_ commands live in freedom_ls.dev_tools and refuse to run unless DEBUG or DEV_TOOLS_ENABLED, so they only ever touch the per-branch dev database; that is strictly less destructive than dev_db_delete.sh, which drops that database outright and is already prompt-free via the scripts wildcard. migrate is deliberately excluded: a destructive migration is the one command here that can cost work someone wanted to keep.
permissions._comment_qa_scripts: Any script placed in .claude/ds/scripts/ or .claude/fls-dev/scripts/ is thereby granted prompt-free QA execution with arbitrary arguments via the Bash(.claude/<plugin>/scripts/*.sh:*) wildcards (in the bare, `./`-prefixed and `bash <script>` invocation forms), and must be reviewed as security-sensitive — equivalent to adding an allow-list entry.
permissions._comment_env_files: Only .env.example may be read or edited. The deny list carries the exact basenames Read(.env) and Edit(.env); every other .env.* basename is refused by the PreToolUse hooks, which exempt .env.example. A glob deny such as Edit(.env.*) cannot be used here: it matches .env.example too and fires before the hook gets a say. The Edit hook also covers Write and NotebookEdit; writes through Bash redirection are not covered by either mechanism.

hooks.command: f=$(jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty'); case "${f##*/}" in .env.example) ;; .env|.env.*) printf '%s' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"Reading .env secret files is blocked; only .env.example may be read."}}' ;; esac

f=$(jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty'); case "${f##*/}" in .env.example) ;; .env|.env.*) printf '%s' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"deny","permissionDecisionReason":"Editing .env secret files is blocked; only .env.example may be edited."}}' ;; esac
